newsitem.title: JAPAN: Family worried about health of freed Japan hostage.
newsitem.headline: Family worried about health of freed Japan hostage.

text.p: The family of Kenji Hirata, the Japanese diplomat who was the latest hostage released by Marxist guerrillas from the siege in Lima, said on Thursday they were worried about his health.
"I got a call from the Foreign Ministry that my son was released," Hirata's mother Yoko told reporters. "I'm worried because he has a weak stomach."
Hirata, 34, was brought out in a wheelchair from the Japanese ambassador's compound, where rebels are still holding 104 hostages, and was immediately taken to a nearby hospital.
In Tokyo, a Foreign Ministry official said Hirata was put on an intravenous drip at the hospital.
"First Secretary Hirata is not sick but exhausted. He said he wants to sleep, so we are having him take a rest," the official told reporters.

"I am happy that he was released," said Hirata's wife, Yuko, 25, who also was briefly a hostage. "But I'm worried that he has become very weak. And I hope all the other hostages will be released soon."
Yuko, who is expecting a baby in March, was in the residence with her husband attending a party to celebrate Emperor Akihito's birthday when the guerrillas took over the building on December 17.
She and all other women were released hours later in the first group of hostages freed by the guerrillas.
Yuko returned immediately to Japan to prepare for the birth of her baby.
Lima is Hirata's first overseas posting.
